argv:
Storage (file attachment) accounting has several problems. How it is meant to work: every uploaded file counts against the plan's storage quota as its own size rounded up to whole megabytes (a 0.3 MB file counts as 1 MB, a 1.5 MB file as 2 MB), and an upload is refused when it would take the workspace past its plan's storage limit (reaching the limit exactly is fine).

1. The storage figure on the billing page does not match the figure uploads are checked against: after uploading a 0.4 MB and a 2.5 MB file, uploads count 4 MB but the billing page shows 3 MB. The billing page and every plan check (including the check made when changing plan) must use exactly the figure uploads are checked against.
2. Deleting files does not give their space back correctly: deleting a file under 1 MB frees nothing, and deleting a 1.5 MB file frees only 1 MB. Deleting a file must give back exactly what it was charged. Deleting a file that does not exist in the workspace (another workspace's file, or one that was already deleted) must fail as not found, the same way other lookups of missing records fail, and must change nothing.
3. Files attached to archived issues cannot be deleted at all (they are reported as not found), and in a workspace with many issues, files on older issues cannot be deleted either. Every file of the workspace must be deletable, whatever the state or age of its issue.
4. The periodic usage recount makes the storage figure jump: after it runs, a workspace's storage no longer matches the running figure, and it can even include storage belonging to other workspaces (one customer deleted enough files to fit the Free plan and still could not downgrade after the recount). The recount must agree with the running figure: the sum, over the workspace's own files, of each file's size rounded up to whole megabytes.
5. When a trial ends, the workspace is moved down to the Free plan unless it has outgrown Free (more members or projects than Free allows), in which case it keeps its plan. Storage is ignored: a trial workspace storing more than Free's storage limit is downgraded anyway. Storing more than Free's storage limit must also keep the workspace on its plan; storing exactly the limit does not.
